title: West Chester Christmas Parade recruits walking marshals for the first time
summary: The Greater West Chester Chamber is adding about 30 marshals who will march inside the Dec. 4 parade alongside floats and bands, on top of the usual 70 sidewalk volunteers. The parade and tree lighting open six weekends of downtown holiday lights.

title: DEP sets Nov. 19 community meeting on the Bishop Tube cleanup
summary: State environmental regulators will present findings from soil and groundwater investigations at the contaminated East Whiteland site and outline next steps for the cleanup, 6-8 p.m. at General Wayne Elementary in Malvern.
loc: Bishop Tube site, East Whiteland Township

title: West Chester's Centinel Spine files to go public on the NYSE
summary: The artificial spinal disc maker filed with the SEC on Oct. 7 to list under the ticker CNTL, which would make it the region's first life sciences IPO since late 2024. The 138-employee company turned a profit in the first half of 2026.

title: WCU president reports progress on the campus Action Plan
summary: In her Oct. 15 fall address, President Laurie Bernotsky highlighted the new One Stop Student Service Center, which has served 500-plus students since opening this fall, and plans for a summer STEM math bridge and an alumni-owned business directory.

title: CCIU opens a new special-education campus in Great Valley Oct. 21
summary: The Chester County Intermediate Unit's purpose-built Child and Career Development Center holds four special-education programs in 12 classrooms and serves students from more than two dozen school districts.

title: East Whiteland hires a PR firm as the data center fight continues
summary: Supervisors approved a short-term contract with Ceisler Media at about $6,800 a month; officials cite a flood of information requests, while residents tie the hire to the proposed 1.5-million-square-foot data center.

title: Residents and Adrian Martinez finish 70 feet of murals at Pinckney Hill Commons
summary: A two-year collaboration led by the Downingtown painter, with dozens of residents and children adding brushwork and handprints, produced three indoor murals at the 51-unit affordable housing community on the Melton Center grounds.

title: Malvern takes up a borough-wide zoning rewrite
summary: Borough Council scheduled a public hearing for Oct. 20 on a full replacement of Malvern's zoning ordinance and map, which would create eight residential districts, two Town Center districts and new open-space and redevelopment zones, with a possible vote the same night.

title: West Goshen zoning rewrite could open the old Boston Market site to housing
summary: The proposed rewrite would move the 1.1-acre E. Gay St. property into a new Mixed Use Corridor district allowing apartments and mixed-use buildings by right. Supervisors are expected to take it up Oct. 20.

title: Chadds Ford's historic Painter's Folly goes to auction Oct. 22
summary: The township is selling the 1857 Italianate house beside Brandywine Battlefield, once home to Howard Pyle's summer art school, after finding ADA upgrades too costly. Conservation and facade easements will protect it under any new owner.
